label: [ Passoff Reading 157 ]

blocks.text: “Liberty is to faction what air is to fire." When he wrote these words, James
Madison clearly expected the faction-ridden nation to produce special-interest
groups constantly pressing for advantage. But even the prescient coauthor of
the Federalist Papers might be amazed at the abundant fulfillment of his
vision by Americans of the present day. The nation has entered a period of
factionalism, a time when the larger desires of society can scarcely be heard
for the insistent clamor of its numberless pieces.
